audits.title: One stop breast clinics--victims of their own success? A prospective audit of referrals to a specialist breast clinic.
audits.setting: Specialist breast clinic, Victoria Infirmary, Glasgow

cycle1.result: 35% of referrals urgent; 28% of urgent and 37% of non-urgent referrals inappropriate according to guidelines.

audits.other_findings: 10% of referrals had breast cancer and 90% benign disease or no pathology.
audits.citation: Patel RS, Smith DC, Reid I. One stop breast clinics--victims of their own success? A prospective audit of referrals to a specialist breast clinic. Eur J Surg Oncol. 2000;26(5):452-454. doi:10.1053/ejso.1999.0920. PMID: 11016464.

audits.title: Has the breast cancer 'two week wait' guarantee for assessment made any difference?
audits.standard: Two-week wait guarantee for suspected breast cancer
audits.setting: Fast Access Breast Clinic, Eastbourne District General Hospital

cycle1.result: Cancer detection 22%; all cancers seen within 1 week; GP referral accuracy 42%; routine wait 4 weeks.

cycle2.result: Cancer detection 19%; 85% seen within 2 weeks; GP accuracy 49%; routine wait at least 8 weeks.

audits.citation: Khawaja AR, Allan SM. Has the breast cancer 'two week wait' guarantee for assessment made any difference?. Eur J Surg Oncol. 2000;26(6):536-539. doi:10.1053/ejso.2000.0942. PMID: 11034802.

audits.title: Audit of referral practice to a fast-access breast clinic before the guaranteed 2-week wait.
audits.setting: Fast-access breast clinic, Eastbourne District General Hospital

cycle1.result: 80% of referrals adhered to guidelines; 73% deemed urgent and seen within 2 weeks; all patients later diagnosed with breast cancer seen within 2 weeks.

audits.other_findings: Suggests specific changes to the referral guidelines.
audits.citation: Khawaja AR, Allan SM. Audit of referral practice to a fast-access breast clinic before the guaranteed 2-week wait. Ann R Coll Surg Engl. 2001;83(1):58-60. PMID: 11212454.

audits.title: Audit of patient's waiting time to see their family doctor prior to referral to a fast-access breast clinic in the era of a guaranteed 2-week wait.
audits.standard: Guaranteed 2-week wait for suspected breast cancer
audits.setting: Fast-access breast clinic, Barnsley District General Hospital

cycle1.result: 40 of 70 patients seen within the 2-week wait; mean wait to see the GP 2.2 days and to see the specialist 6.6 days.

audits.other_findings: 20 were classed urgent, 20 soon and 30 routine; 12 were clinically malignant; fast-track referral was not appropriate in all cases.
audits.citation: Agaba AE, Bagul A, Adenugba JB, Kenogbon JI. Audit of patient's waiting time to see their family doctor prior to referral to a fast-access breast clinic in the era of a guaranteed 2-week wait. Breast. 2002;11(5):430-433. doi:10.1054/brst.2002.0449. PMID: 14965707.

audits.title: A Single-Center Audit of Symptomatic Breast Cancer Patient Referrals During COVID-19 Pandemic Restrictions.
audits.standard: Two-week wait specialist consultation for suspected breast cancer
audits.setting: Oncoplastic breast surgery unit, Princess Royal University Hospital, Telford

cycle1.result: 2019 cohort: 1564 referrals; breast cancer diagnosis rate 4.9%.

audits.intervention: COVID-19 service restrictions including telephone consultations (not a planned improvement).

cycle2.result: Referrals fell by 442 (28.3%); higher rate of two-week specialist consultation (p < 0.05); cancer diagnosis 6.9%.

audits.other_findings: Of 521 telephone consultations, 29.2% discharged and 70.4% needed one-stop clinic visits, 9.0% of whom had cancer.
audits.citation: Tokode OM, Rastall S. A Single-Center Audit of Symptomatic Breast Cancer Patient Referrals During COVID-19 Pandemic Restrictions. Cureus. 2022;14(6):e26038. doi:10.7759/cureus.26038. PMID: 35734027.
